notes: The tutorial has two wiring diagrams (burn bootloader; upload via USB-serial). I built the first: the bootloader-burning (ArduinoISP) circuit with the external 16 MHz clock. The upload circuit (RX/TX wires, Arduino microcontroller removed) and the minimal no-crystal circuit are not included.
The 10k pull-up resistor from ATmega pin 1 (RESET) to +5V is drawn in the image and listed in the parts list.
Arduino pin 10 goes to ATmega pin 1 (RESET), pin 11 to pin 17 (MOSI), pin 12 to pin 18 (MISO), pin 13 to pin 19 (SCK), as in the standard ArduinoISP wiring.
The crystal sits across ATmega pins 9 and 10 (XTAL1/XTAL2) via the two blue wires; each 22 pF capacitor goes from a crystal leg to ground.
Exact breadboard hole positions and rail indices are estimated from the picture. The chip straddles the centre gap, with pins 1-14 on the bottom half and 15-28 on the top half.

The image shows no clear AVCC (pin 20) or second GND (pin 22 is grounded, pin 8 also) wire beyond what is drawn. I added only the visible power wires: +5V to pin 7 and GND to pins 8 and 22. A real build should also connect pin 20 (AVCC) to +5V.
Top rail 'tp' is +5V and 'tn' is GND, linked to the bottom rails 'bp' and 'bn' by the long red and black wires on the right.
